title: Tenet quest file (the legacy one-file format)
description: The one-file format, still read: one file under config/tenet/quests/ holding a whole questline. New packs should use the folder format instead - one group.json, one chapter.json and one quest per file - whose schemas are the `_schema/` set beside this one. A questline may be split across any number of these; the loader treats them as one tree and dependencies resolve across files.

$schema.description: Ignored by Tenet. For your editor, so it can autocomplete the rest of this file.

version.description: Format version. Written into new files. Present from the first release so that a future change has something to migrate from.

text.description: Either a plain string, or a translation key with an English fallback.

fallback.description: Shown if the translation is missing. Without it a player sees the raw key.

itemRef.description: An item, a count, and optional data components. Not an ItemStack — resolved at the moment it is used.

item.description: Namespaced item id, e.g. minecraft:oak_log. An item this build does not have keeps its id and the quest still loads: the row draws a placeholder and says the item is missing, so a removed mod can come back.

components.description: 1.21 data components, keyed by component id in the datapack's own spelling. A text component's value is a string holding JSON, as the codec writes it -- { "minecraft:custom_name": "\"Tempered Pickaxe\"" } -- and the editor writes that form when you pick a renamed item. Matched strictly: a task naming a renamed sword wants that sword and not a plain one.

icon.description: What a quest, chapter, group or the book shows as its picture: an item, a texture file, an atlas region, or an entity drawn as its spawn egg. An item object is the arm every file written before the union uses, so old files read unchanged.

texture.description: A texture file by its own path, e.g. my_pack:textures/gui/emblem.png. Drawn stretched into the icon's box; a path nothing holds draws the missing texture.

sprite.description: An atlas region id, e.g. minecraft:block/sculk. Drawn from the atlas into the icon's box; a region nothing holds draws the missing mark.

entity.description: An entity id, e.g. minecraft:creeper. Drawn as its spawn egg where one exists; an entity with no egg draws the missing mark naming it.

id.description: Lowercase letters, digits and underscores. This id appears in player progress files, so changing it needs an entry in `aliases`.

alias.description: A former id, in any letter case. Lookups ignore case, so an uppercase alias resolves the same object; ids themselves stay lowercase.

namespacedId.description: A namespaced id, e.g. minecraft:oak_log or my_pack:chapter_one. The namespace is required, as it is everywhere this format names something by id.

stageId.description: A stage id: namespaced like my_pack:left_the_village, or a bare GameStages-style word like completed_pyramid. A bare word reads under the minecraft: namespace, the way Minecraft reads every id without one. Prefer an explicit namespace for pack-owned stages; keep the bare spelling for stages migrating over from GameStages.

dependencyStyle.description: One line's style. Only the axes it names override anything; the axes it omits fall back to the chapter's default, and then to the built-ins (chamfered, chevron at the target, solid, thin).

form.description: The route's shape. Chamfered is the built-in default: the three-segment step with every 90-degree corner cut at 45 degrees, a circuit trace. Orthogonal is the same step left square, straight a direct line, and curved a smooth bow, which reads `bend`.

arrowHead.description: The glyph an arrowhead is drawn as. Chevron is the built-in; none is a blunt line end.

arrowPlace.description: Where the heads sit: one at the dependent end (the built-in), one at each end, one in the middle of the route, or a repeating run.

arrowDensity.description: How far apart a stream repeats: 64, 32 or 16 pixels. Ignored by the other placements.

arrows.description: Legacy, read but no longer written: the single axis the three arrow axes replaced. None is a blunt end, one a chevron at the target, both one at each end, and many a stream at its old 24-pixel spacing.

dash.description: The line's pattern. Double is two hairlines either side of the route and ignores `weight`; hazard is the run plus diagonal hatch marks.

weight.description: How many pixels wide: 1, 2, 3, or a 6-pixel conduit with dark borders around a lighter core.

bend.description: How far a curved line bows, as a fraction of the chord between its ends. Positive bows one way and negative the other.

fromAnchor.description: The angle this line leaves its source node at, in degrees, 0 east and growing clockwise. Per line only. Absent means the automatic rim point.

toAnchor.description: The angle this line meets its target node at, in degrees, 0 east and growing clockwise. Per line only. Absent means the automatic rim point.

fromHandle.description: A split line's source-side control point, as [along, across] fractions of the line's own chord. `fromHandle` and `toHandle` are written together - one alone is a split with half a shape.

toHandle.description: A split line's target-side control point, as [along, across] fractions of the line's own chord.

themePatch.description: Token-level overrides for a chapter's theme: individual palette colours, a corner radius and a canvas background, applied over the named theme (or over the player's own when the chapter names none). A client concept, like `theme` itself - the server carries it and the client composes it. The validator checks every token id and value with the toolkit's own reader.

name.description: A name for the resulting palette. Usually omitted - the Chapter tab writes none, and the name only matters for a file that also wants a display name.

colours.description: Token id to colour, e.g. { "raised": "#FF24242E" }. A colour is #RRGGBB, #AARRGGBB, or a bare 0xAARRGGBB number. An unknown token id is reported by the validator, and the client ignores it.

canvasBackground.description: A pattern over the canvas's colour - the same object a theme file carries. `spacing` is content units under `graph` and screen pixels under `screen`; an image is screen-fixed and ignores it. The ink is the `canvasPattern` colour token, whose alpha is a pattern's strength - an image uses only its alpha and draws in white.

space.description: What the pattern is anchored to: the content, or the screen. Ignored by `image`, which is always screen-fixed.

spacing.description: Distance between repeats. Clamped to this range by the reader.

size.description: The edge of a dot or speck and the thickness of a line or hatch step, in pixels. Clamped to this range by the reader.

density.description: Speckle only: one cell in this many carries a mark. Clamped to this range by the reader.

direction.description: Hatch only: which way the diagonal leans.

fit.description: Image only: repeat the texture at `tile` size, or draw it once scaled to cover and centred.

texture.description: Image only: the texture id, canonicalised to `ns:textures/path.png`. An unresolvable texture draws nothing.

tile.description: Image only, under `tile` fit: the width one repeat is drawn at, in pixels. Clamped to this range by the reader.

cornerRadius.description: Corner radius in pixels for the chapter's surfaces. Zero is square.

motion.description: Transition duration in milliseconds. Zero disables transitions.

rewardTable.description: A roll of rewards: the table an inline-table reward carries. A weight-zero entry is always granted, once per roll call; every positive weight shares the rest of the probability space, and `lootSize` is how many times the dice are thrown.

emptyWeight.description: The chance of nothing on a throw, against the positive weights. Only tenet:loot includes it: a tenet:random promises something.

lootSize.description: How many times the dice are thrown.

title.description: What the table is called in the editor and on a reward's badge. Absent or blank falls back to the id, opened out: `tier_1_ores` reads as "Tier 1 ores".

icon.description: The item a browser row or a reward badge draws for this table. Absent means the first entry that has an item, then that entry's reward type's icon.

uid.description: The editor's handle for a table written `inline` in a quest or in another table: it is what the editor addresses when a reward sits above or below it in a list. A table in its own file under `reward_tables/` is addressed by its file name, does not use this, and the loader ignores it there.

useTitle.description: Draw this table's title on a reward row that rolls it, rather than the generic roll sentence. The legacy format calls this use_title.

hideTooltip.description: Draw no item tooltip on a reward row that rolls this table. The legacy format calls this hide_tooltip.

weight.description: How much of the table's weight this entry takes. Zero means always granted, which is how a table says "and everyone also gets this".

reward.description: The reward this entry grants. All of anyType except two things. `conditions` cannot mean anything here: an entry is handed out by the roll rather than claimed, so a gate on it would be validated and then ignored. And `tenet:choice` cannot be an entry at all: a roll hands its entries out rather than offering them, so a choice entry is skipped. Put conditions on the table reward itself, and a choice on a quest.

condition.description: A gate on a task or a reward: every entry of a `conditions` list must hold for a player before the task counts for them, or the reward is paid to them. An empty list is met by definition.

type.description: The condition type's id, e.g. tenet:stage. The id decides which of the fields below mean anything.

count.description: tenet:item and tenet:item_tag (condition) — how many of them.

components.description: tenet:item (condition) — 1.21 data components, as on a task's item.

match.description: tenet:item (condition) — how closely a carried stack must match.

tag.description: tenet:item_tag (condition) — an item tag; any item in it counts.

objective.description: tenet:score (condition) — the scoreboard objective's name. An objective that does not exist reads as zero, so a typo locks the gate.

min.description: tenet:score and tenet:party_size (condition) — the number to reach: a score, or the members of the party online now. At least 1, so an objective that does not exist (which reads as 0) locks the gate rather than opening it. tenet:party_size is capped at 1000; tenet:score has no ceiling.

advancement.description: tenet:advancement (condition) — the advancement to have earned.

criterion.description: tenet:advancement (condition) — require one criterion of it instead of the whole advancement.

stage.description: tenet:stage (condition) — the stage to have, bare or namespaced.

oneOf.description: One string per paragraph. Also accepts a bare string, for a one-line description. Markdown is read in these strings: **bold**, *italic*, `code`, [links](https://example.com), `#` headings and `- ` bullets.

description.description: A list of paragraphs, as a chapter's and a quest's are. A bare string is also accepted.

aliases.description: Former ids. Add one when renaming, and nothing that referenced the old name breaks.

tags.description: Words this group answers to in lookups by tag. Each tag is lowercase letters, digits and underscores, the same rule an id follows. The legacy format calls this tags, present on every object.

icon.description: The item the book draws on the group's row. Optional: an absent icon falls back to the first chapter under the group.

collapsedByDefault.description: Whether the group starts folded in the sidebar. A reference group nobody reads front to back sets this; a player's own fold state is remembered over it.

element.description: One thing drawn on the chapter's canvas that is not a quest. `type` chooses which of the fields below apply; `id`, `order`, `dev` and `requires` apply to every type. Elements are drawn beneath the quest nodes and the dependency lines, ordered among themselves by `order` and then by the order they are written in this array. Nothing here is counted for the chapter's completion and nothing here gates anything: an element is a label on the map rather than a place on it.

type.description: Which kind of element this is. image is a picture drawn from a file or from a region of the block atlas; text is a label; line is a rule with an optional arrowhead at either end; rect is a filled box with an optional border. A type this build does not know is kept, reported once as a warning, and draws nothing - so a chapter from a newer build still loads.

id.description: Unique within this chapter, and the name a translation key uses (`element.<id>.text` for a label's words, `element.<id>.title` for a picture's). Two elements sharing one is reported, because the second could then never be addressed.

order.description: Draw order among this chapter's elements, ascending. Two elements with the same order keep the order they are written in this array, which is why a plain label needs no number at all.

dev.description: Drawn only while the editor's dev mode is on, and only for somebody who may edit. How an author drafts a layout without shipping it: a reader with dev mode off never sees it.

requires.description: A quest id or alias: the element is drawn only once that quest is completed. A name that resolves to nothing is reported at load, because the element would then never be drawn at all. Note that this reads a quest's state and changes nothing about it - an element is never a dependency.

x.description: image, text and rect: the left edge in canvas pixels, measured the same way a quest node's `x` is. The migration tool converts the legacy centre-based coordinates to this corner.

y.description: image, text and rect: the top edge in canvas pixels. For a text label this is the top of its first line.

x1.description: line: the first endpoint's x, in canvas pixels.

width.description: image and rect: how wide, in canvas pixels (1 to 4096 for a picture, 1 to 8192 for a box). line: how thick the stroke is, 1 to 16, which the arrowhead is also sized by. A picture or a box is stretched to fill its rectangle; nothing preserves an aspect ratio.

height.description: image and rect: how tall, in canvas pixels, bounded exactly as `width` is.

rotation.description: image: degrees clockwise. Wrapped rather than clamped, so -90, 270 and 630 are all one quarter turn - a clamped -90 would be no turn at all, which is the opposite of what the file says. Turned about the element's centre, or about its own top-left when `corner` is true.

corner.description: image: turn about this element's own top-left corner instead of its centre. The legacy format calls this alignToCorner, and it is what a logo pinned by its corner needs - the two pivots are visibly different pictures.

locked.description: image: pin the picture against the editor's drag - grips and moves leave it where it is. Readers are unaffected. The legacy format calls this position_locked, and the migration tool maps it onto this key.

tint.description: image: a colour multiplied into the picture, alpha included. White leaves it exactly as authored.

alpha.description: image: 0 to 255, multiplied with `tint`'s own alpha. the legacy format carries the two separately, so both are kept and neither is lost in conversion.

title.description: image: a hover tooltip, or words painted into the picture when `label.onImage` is set. For a label's own words see `text` below.

text.description: text: the words. A newline starts a second line. Plain text with no markup - there is no emphasis in this format, so asterisks stay asterisks.

scale.description: text: the size of the words, 0.25 to 4.0, multiplied by the player's own text-scale setting on top.

color.description: text and line: the ink. A colour is #RRGGBB, #AARRGGBB, or a number read as the same 32-bit pattern.

shadow.description: text: draw the font's own drop shadow under the words. Off by default, because a label with a backdrop behind it does not want one - on is for a label floating over a chapter, where there is no backdrop to draw.

fixed.description: text: fix the size to the canvas - positioned with the canvas like anything on it, but drawn at the file's own size times the zoom, the way a node is. Off by default, when the size stays the file's own on screen at every zoom.

arrowhead.description: line: which ends carry an arrowhead. none is a blunt rule. This is its own vocabulary rather than the dependency lines' placement, because a free line means nothing and the only question is which way it points.

fillColor.description: rect: the fill, drawn first. A colour is #RRGGBB, #AARRGGBB, or a number. The default is fully transparent, so a box that names no colour draws nothing - the editor's own "add a box" writes a visible one.

borderColor.description: rect: the border, drawn over the fill.

borderWidth.description: rect: how thick the border is, 0 to 16. Zero draws none, which is the default.

imageSource.description: Where a picture comes from: exactly one of a file or a region of the block atlas. The two are different lookups that fail differently - a file that is not there draws nothing, and a sprite the atlas does not hold draws the game's missing-texture marker - so which one is meant is written down rather than inferred from a suffix.

texture.description: A PNG by its own path, e.g. atm:textures/questpics/logo.png. Note the textures/ directory and the .png are part of it: this is a file's path, not an item's.

sprite.description: A region of the block atlas, e.g. minecraft:block/sculk or powah:item/uraninite_raw. Which sheet to look it up in is the reader's business, not the file's.

elementLabel.description: How a picture's title is painted into it, rather than shown on hover. Each field has a legacy counterpart, so a converted chapter's text_on_image, text_shadow, text_inset, text_h_align and text_v_align all land here.

onImage.description: Whether the title is drawn into the picture at all. Off means it is a hover tooltip, which is what a title usually wants.

shadow.description: Draw the words with the font's own shadow, for a picture whose area behind them is busy or bright.

inset.description: How far the words sit from the edge their alignment names, in pixels, 0 to 64.

hAlign.description: Where the words sit across the picture: against its left edge, centred, or against its right.

click.description: What pressing an element does. All seven names the legacy format can write are readable here, and all seven run: a command through the server's dispatcher, an event through the script bus, a recipe through a viewer, a guide page as a message, a quest or a page straight.

type.description: What a press does. none is an element that is not pressable; open_quest opens another quest by id or alias; open_uri opens an http or https address in the browser; show_recipe opens the item's recipes in a viewer, or says there is none installed; show_docs names a guide page, which has no integration and answers with a message; run_command runs server-side as the pressing player at the pack's level; custom_event fires a script event by id.

data.description: What the action acts on: a quest id or alias for open_quest, an http or https URL for open_uri, an item id for show_recipe, mod and book for show_docs, a command for run_command, an event id for custom_event. Unused by none.

link.description: One marker pointing at another quest. Drawn in the node layer with the target's state and icon; pressing it opens that quest. A link is never counted for its chapter's completion and no dependency, gate or milestone may name one.

id.description: Unique within this chapter, and never equal to any quest, chapter or group id or alias: two nodes addressed by one name means a press opens whichever the lookup finds first.

quest.description: The target quest, by id or alias, in any chapter. A name that resolves to nothing is reported at load, because the link would then mirror nothing and its press would do nothing. The legacy format calls this linked_quest, and the migration tool maps it onto this key.

x.description: The left edge in canvas pixels, measured the same way a quest node's `x` is. The migration tool converts the legacy centre-based doubles to this corner.

y.description: The top edge in canvas pixels.

shape.description: The node's shape. Absent draws as the target quest does.

size.description: The node's size in pixels, 16 to 512. Absent draws at the target quest's size.

description.description: One string per paragraph. Separate from a single newline-containing string on purpose. Markdown is read in these strings.

tags.description: Words this chapter answers to in lookups by tag. Each tag is lowercase letters, digits and underscores, the same rule an id follows. The legacy format calls this tags, present on every object.

progressionMode.description: In a linear chapter the order of the quests list *is* the progression: each unlocks when the one above it completes, and no dependsOn is needed. A quest in a linear chapter that also declares dependsOn must satisfy *both*: the quest above it and its own edges. That is a real combination rather than a mistake — a linear spine with one quest that also needs something from another chapter — so nothing warns about it.

defaultPrerequisiteMode.description: What every quest in this chapter uses unless it says otherwise.

defaultConsumeItems.description: Whether item tasks in this chapter take the items unless the task says otherwise. The inherited default, which is why it lives here: an author sets it once for a whole trade chapter.

defaultFlexibleProgress.description: Whether this chapter's quests may work their tasks before their dependencies are met, unless a quest says otherwise. Either this or a quest's flexibleProgress makes the quest flexible.

defaultMinWidth.description: What the quests in this chapter use for their detail-panel width unless a quest says otherwise: a quest's own minWidth wins over this, and 0 (unset) means the panel kind decides. The legacy format calls this default_min_width.

autofocus.description: The quest this chapter centres on when it is selected, by id or alias, in this chapter. Absent centres on the chapter's bounding box. The legacy format calls this autofocus_id.

autoClaim.description: Whether this chapter's quests hand their rewards over on completion. `enabled` pays with a notification, `no_toast` silently, and `invisible` the same silence - the two silent names grant alike, the difference being the legacy vocabulary rather than a behaviour; `disabled` waits for a claim, and `default` defers to the pack setting in index.json. A quest overrides this, and a reward's own `auto` overrides that. Rewards that need a decision - a choice reward - are never auto-granted whatever this says.

dependencyStyle.description: How this chapter's dependency lines are drawn unless a line overrides an axis. This is what a line's "Use chapter default" resets to. Only the axes named here are chosen: an axis left out falls back to the built-ins (chamfered, one, solid, thin), and a line that names the same axis overrides just that one.

dependsOn.description: The chapters this one waits on, by id or alias. Until the rule below is met every quest in this chapter is locked - it cannot be started, finished or claimed - whatever its own dependsOn says. A name that resolves to nothing is reported at load, because the chapter could then never be opened. The folder format's chapter.json carries the same fields.

prerequisiteMode.description: The rule over this chapter's own dependsOn, and *not* defaultPrerequisiteMode: that one is the mode this chapter's quests inherit for their quest dependencies, and this one is how many of the chapters above must be satisfied. all_completed is the default because a gate that let something through early is the surprising direction to be wrong in.

minRequired.description: How many of dependsOn must be satisfied, replacing the mode's own count - "any two of these three chapters". May not exceed the size of dependsOn, which is reported. It replaces the count and not the bar: the mode still decides whether a dependency has to be completed or merely started.

completesWhen.description: The quests that finish this chapter, by id or alias, in any chapter. The chapter reports completed once every one of them is; a repeatable quest counts after its first completion. Empty means the chapter never reports completed, which is a real state - it is then only ever satisfiable as "started". A chapter another chapter waits on as completed must declare this, and the loader reports the pair that does not.

hideUntilDependenciesComplete.description: Whether this chapter is left out of the book for a reader until its own dependencies are met. Off, it is listed and drawn dimmed with what it is waiting for on hover. An author in edit mode always sees it, or the flag could not be authored. Presentation only: the gate itself is enforced whatever this says. Not the same field as defaultHideUntilDependenciesComplete below: this one withholds the chapter's row, those decide what its quests do.

alwaysInvisible.description: Whether this chapter is withheld from every reader, whatever its gate says. Beside hideUntilDependenciesComplete because they are the pair an author will confuse: that one withholds the row until the gate is met, this one withholds it always. The gate itself is unaffected. The legacy format calls this always_invisible.

disableCanvasLod.description: Whether this chapter's canvas draws without the zoom tiers: icons, rings, titles and badges at any zoom. Absent defers to the book's own flag; present `true` draws everything always, present `false` keeps the tiers even when the book disables them.

defaultHideUntilDependenciesComplete.description: What the quests in this chapter do about their own prerequisites unless a quest says otherwise: with it on, a quest here is hidden until its own prerequisite rule is met. A quest may write false to opt out, and a quest with no prerequisites is visible either way.

defaultHideUntilDependenciesVisible.description: The same default for hideUntilDependenciesVisible: with it on, a quest here is hidden until at least one of its prerequisites is itself visible.

theme.description: A palette this chapter asks to be drawn in. A client concept: the catalogue of themes lives on the client, so this is a plain string here and is reported by the client that could not resolve it.

themePatch.description: Token-level overrides for `theme`: individual colours and a corner radius applied over the named theme (or over the player's own when no theme is named). This is how a chapter sets "raised #24242E and radius 4" without shipping a whole theme file, and the Chapter tab's appearance section writes it.

elements.description: What is drawn *under* this chapter's quests: a picture, a label, a rule or a box. The chapter's own file carries them in the folder format too, so this is the same field in the same place - the one-file format is read by the same codec, which is why an element here works exactly as it does there.

links.description: Markers pointing at other quests: each draws in the node layer with its target's state and icon, and pressing it opens that quest. The folder format's chapter.json carries the same field in the same place - the one-file format is read by the same codec, which is why a link here works exactly as it does there.

tags.description: Words this quest answers to in lookups by tag. Each tag is lowercase letters, digits and underscores, the same rule an id follows. A lookup of `#tag` resolves to the first quest, chapter or group carrying it. The legacy format calls this tags, present on every object.

guidePage.description: The guide book page this quest belongs to. A reference the quest card shows; Tenet has no guide integration, so nothing reads it further. Empty means absent. The legacy format calls this guide_page.

dependsOn.description: Quest ids or aliases. May refer to quests in other files. A reference that resolves to nothing is an error: the quest could never unlock.

dependencyLines.description: Per-line overrides, keyed by the id of the dependency the line comes from. Only the axes named for a line are overridden; the rest fall back to the chapter's `dependencyStyle`, and then to the built-ins. A key that names a dependency the quest does not have is dead weight, and the editor drops an entry once it sets nothing.

prerequisiteMode.description: Overrides the chapter's setting for this quest.

minRequired.description: How many dependencies must be satisfied, replacing the mode's own count: this is how "any three of these five" is written. The mode still decides the *bar* each one must reach — completed, or merely started — so `one_started` with minRequired 2 means "any two of these, started". May not exceed the number of dependencies.

x.description: Canvas position. The shipped chapters sit on a 32-unit grid; the editor snaps to 8.

shape.description: The node's outline, each drawn at its own true proportions. "none" draws no panel at all: the node is its icon, and the whole square is clickable. Every other outline is hit-tested by its own pixels, so a click lands on exactly what is drawn.

rotation.description: How far the node is turned, in degrees clockwise. Every shape can be turned: a rotation rotates the outline rather than naming a second one, and the node is drawn, clicked and icon-fitted in its turned form. A turned outline is fitted to the node with one uniform scale, so nothing is cut off at the node's edge and nothing is stretched. A full turn is written as 0, because it is the same shape.

iconScale.description: How much of the node the icon fills. The outline caps it: a shape with less room draws the largest item it can hold, so the frames stay comparable. 1.0 is corner to corner; the default leaves a margin so the node's shape reads.

showTitle.description: Draw this quest's name under its node. Off by default: a canvas of fifty names is a wall of text, and the name is on hover for every quest either way.

sequentialTasks.description: Tasks must be done in order: the second cannot be handed in until the first is.

optional.description: This quest does not gate its dependants: they count it as neither satisfied nor required, so it neither helps nor blocks them. Dependency lines from it are still drawn. For side quests and branches nothing waits for.

flexibleProgress.description: Tasks may be worked on before this quest's dependencies are met; completion waits for them. Either this or the chapter's defaultFlexibleProgress makes the quest flexible.

autoClaim.description: Whether this quest's rewards are handed over the moment it completes, overriding the chapter's own `autoClaim` (which in turn defers to the pack setting in index.json). A reward's own `auto` still wins over this. `enabled` pays with a notification, `no_toast` silently, `invisible` with no trace; `disabled` waits for a claim. Rewards that need a decision - a choice reward - are never auto-granted whatever this says.

repeatCooldownTicks.description: Ticks to wait between completions of a repeatable quest. 2400 is two minutes.

exclusiveGroup.description: Quests sharing a group name are mutually exclusive: completing one locks the others for good. Scoped to the chapter.

repeatable.description: Completable more than once. Its timesCompleted survives each completion, and something depending on it stays satisfied.

invisibleUntilTasks.description: With `invisible` also set: shown once this many of the quest's tasks have any progress, as well as when it is completed. The easter-egg case — a quest nobody can see until they have stumbled onto part of it. Without `invisible` it does nothing.

maxCompletableDependents.description: At most this many of the quests that depend on this one may complete; the rest stay locked for good. 0 is no cap. A branch point: the player picks one way, and the other ways close. A dependent already completed stays completed.

hideUntilDependenciesComplete.description: Hidden until this quest's prerequisite *rule* is satisfied — the same rule the card's "2 of 3 met" counts, so minRequired and the started-based modes are honoured. A completed quest is always visible. Leave the field out and the chapter's defaultHideUntilDependenciesComplete decides; write false to opt out of a chapter that hides its quests by default.

hideUntilDependenciesVisible.description: Hidden until at least one of its prerequisites is itself visible. Recursive, so a chain of hidden quests reveals itself one link at a time from its first visible end. A quest with no prerequisites at all is visible, because an empty rule is met - this used to stay hidden, which is the trap the sibling flag's empty case never had. Leave the field out and the chapter's defaultHideUntilDependenciesVisible decides; write false to opt out.

hideDependencyLines.description: Draw no dependency lines arriving at this quest. The quest itself is unaffected, and quests that depend on it still draw their lines to it.

hideDependentLines.description: Draw no dependency lines leaving this quest for its dependants. The outgoing half of hideDependencyLines. The legacy format calls this hide_dependent_lines.

minWidth.description: Minimum width of this quest's detail panel. 0 is unset: the chapter's defaultMinWidth decides, and then the panel kind's default. The legacy format calls this min_width.

disableToast.description: Completing this quest raises no toast. Combines with the silent auto-claim modes: either silence wins. The legacy format calls this disable_toast.

ignoreRewardBlocking.description: This quest's rewards keep flowing while the team's payouts are held. Either the quest's flag or a reward's own flag exempts that reward. The legacy format calls this ignore_reward_blocking.

disableRecipeMod.description: Recipe viewers (JEI, REI, EMI) do not list this quest. Leave the field out and the file's `defaultDisableRecipeMod` decides; write `false` to opt out of a file that hides its quests by default. The legacy format calls this disable_recipe_mod.

hideLockIcon.description: This quest wears no padlock on the canvas when it is locked: the quest's half of the file's `showLockIcons`. Either silence wins, and absent defers to the file. The legacy format calls this hide_lock_icon.

hideTextUntilComplete.description: The reader's card shows no description until the quest is completed — for a quest whose text would give away what it is asking for. The editor always shows it.

hideDetailsUntilStartable.description: The reader's card shows no task or reward details until the quest can be started. REQUIRES stays: a locked quest's prerequisites are what says how to unlock it. The editor always shows everything.

requiresStage.description: A stage the player must have for the quest to be open to them, e.g. my_pack:chapter_one or a bare completed_pyramid. The one gate here that is per player rather than per team: a quest gated on a stage is open to a player who has it and locked to one who does not, even in the same party. Nothing validates that the stage exists -- one exists by being granted -- so a typo shows up as a quest nobody can open.

requiresStageTeam.description: Read the quest's requiresStage gate from the team's stages rather than the player's own. One member's induction then opens the quest for everybody. The legacy format calls this team_stage.

anyType.description: A task or a reward. The `type` field chooses the rest of the fields, and each field below names the type it belongs to. A field written for another type is a mistake the validator reports rather than a value anything reads.

type.description: The type's id, e.g. tenet:item. The id decides which of the fields below mean anything.

optional.description: Tasks only. An optional task does not have to be done for the quest to complete, unless every task is optional.

autoSubmitTicks.description: Tasks only. How often the task is re-checked, in ticks, twenty to the second. Left out, the task keeps its type's own cadence — 20 for most, 3 for a stat or a location, 5 for an advancement, 100 for a dimension — which is a sensible interval for how expensive that check is. Set it to override that. There is deliberately no one default here: a single number would be wrong for most of the types it applied to.

conditions.description: Tasks and rewards. Gates that must all hold for a player before the task counts for them, or the reward is paid to them.

disableToast.description: Tasks and rewards. This task finishing, or this reward collected, raises no toast. The legacy format calls this disable_toast.

title.description: Tasks and rewards. The words the row wears instead of the type's own sentence. Absent means the type decides. A checkmark's title is its button's text.

icon.description: Tasks and rewards. The picture the row wears instead of the type's own: an item, a texture file, an atlas region, or an entity drawn as its spawn egg. Absent means the type decides.

tags.description: Tasks and rewards. Words this row answers to in lookups by tag. Each tag is lowercase letters, digits and underscores, the same rule an id follows. The legacy format calls this tags, present on every object.

item.description: tenet:item (task and reward) — the item to hand over, or to give.

count.description: tenet:item and tenet:item_tag (tasks), tenet:item (reward) — how many.

components.description: tenet:item (task and reward) — 1.21 data components, keyed by component id in the datapack's own spelling. A text component's value is a string holding JSON, as the codec writes it -- the editor writes that form when you pick a renamed item.

consumeItems.description: tenet:item and tenet:item_tag (tasks) — whether handing the task in takes the items. Falls back to the chapter's defaultConsumeItems.

match.description: tenet:item (task) — how closely a carried stack must match: none ignores its data, fuzzy needs the data it names, strict needs the whole stack. Strict is the default, so a file that says nothing keeps the meaning it had before this field existed.

onlyFromCrafting.description: tenet:item and tenet:item_tag (tasks) — only items the player crafted themselves count. Counted from lifetime crafting statistics, so handing the stack away does not un-count it.

manualOnly.description: tenet:item, tenet:item_tag, tenet:filter, tenet:fluid and tenet:energy (tasks) — never count from the inventory on the tick; only a submit press counts. The legacy format calls this task_screen_only, filled by piping into a task screen; Tenet has no such block, so the piped path is not ported.

maxInput.description: tenet:energy (task) — the most each item may contribute, in Forge Energy units; 0 means unlimited. The legacy format calls this max_input, capping each insertion into its task screen.

tag.description: tenet:item_tag (task) — an item tag; any item in it counts.

dimension.description: tenet:dimension and tenet:location (tasks) — the dimension the player has to be in, or the one the location box is in.

biome.description: tenet:biome (task) — the biome to stand in; a #tag counts any biome of it.

structure.description: tenet:structure (task) — the structure to be inside; a #tag counts any of them.

advancement.description: tenet:advancement (task and reward) — the advancement to earn, or to award.

criterion.description: tenet:advancement (task and reward) — one criterion of it instead of the whole advancement; empty for the whole one.

stat.description: tenet:stat (task) — which vanilla statistic to watch.

value.description: tenet:stat, tenet:xp, tenet:kill, tenet:break, tenet:energy and tenet:custom (tasks) — the number that counts as enough: the statistic's value, experience or energy handed over, kills, breaks, or the handler's count.

ignoreDimension.description: tenet:location (task) — count the box anywhere, instead of only in the dimension above.

position.description: tenet:location (task) — one corner of the box, in blocks, as [x, y, z].

size.description: tenet:location (task) — how far the box reaches from that corner, as [x, y, z].

points.description: tenet:xp (task) — whether the count is experience points (true, the default) or whole levels (false).

fluid.description: tenet:fluid (task) — the fluid to hand over, carried in buckets.

filter.description: tenet:filter (task) — which items count, as a legacy filter expression: item, item_tag, mod and block leaves under and, or and not, e.g. or(item(minecraft:coal)item_tag(minecraft:coals)). Passed through verbatim from an ftbfiltersystem:smart_filter stack.

amount.description: tenet:fluid (task) — how much of it, in millibuckets; a bucket is a thousand. tenet:xp (reward) — points, or levels, to give.

observeType.description: tenet:observation (task) — what counts as looking: a block, a tag of them, one block state, a block entity, or an entity. The target below follows this.

toObserve.description: tenet:observation (task) — the block or entity to look at.

timer.description: tenet:observation (task) — how long to look at it, in ticks, twenty to the second.

entityTypeTag.description: tenet:kill (task) — or an entity tag, to count any mob in it. Its own field rather than a # in `entity`, so a tag where an id is expected is an error here as it is everywhere else.

customName.description: tenet:kill (task) — only counts a mob with this name.

nbtFilter.description: tenet:kill (task) — an SNBT filter, for the mobs an id cannot pick out.

blockTag.description: tenet:break (task) — or a block tag, to count any block in it. Its own field rather than a # in `block`, so a tag where an id is expected is an error here as it is everywhere else.

blockState.description: tenet:break (task) — only count this block state, e.g. minecraft:wheat[age=7], for what an id cannot pick out. Narrows `block` or `blockTag`, or stands alone.

id.description: tenet:custom (task and reward) — the id a mod or a script registered a handler for. The validator warns when this build has nothing registered for it.

team.description: Rewards only. Whether this is a one-claim-for-the-team reward. Absent falls back to the tree's defaultTeamReward.

auto.description: Rewards only. When it is handed over: default follows the tree's own setting, enabled gives it on completion, disabled waits for a claim, no_toast gives it without a toast, and invisible grants the same way - the two silent names are the legacy vocabulary rather than a behaviour.

excludeFromClaimAll.description: Rewards only. Claim all leaves this one for its own press.

ignoreRewardBlocking.description: Rewards only. Give it even while the team's rewards are being held.

randomBonus.description: tenet:item (reward) — up to this many more, rolled at random on top of the count.

onlyOne.description: tenet:item (reward) — skip it if the player already carries this item.

levels.description: tenet:xp (reward) — give whole levels rather than points, which is the default. The task's own switch is `points`, and it reads the other way: true there counts points.

table.description: tenet:random, tenet:loot, tenet:all_table and tenet:choice (rewards) — the reward table to roll, by id: a file under reward_tables/, named without its .json suffix. The roll happens when the reward is collected.

inline.description: tenet:random, tenet:loot, tenet:all_table and tenet:choice (rewards) — the table itself, for a reward that is its own roll.

permissionLevel.description: tenet:command (reward) — the permission level the command runs at; 2 is a command block's.

command.description: tenet:command (reward) — run as the player when the reward is collected, without the leading slash.

silent.description: tenet:command (reward) — do not say in chat that it ran.

feedbackMessage.description: tenet:command (reward) — a message shown when the command runs; absent shows nothing extra. The legacy format calls this feedback_message.

description.description: tenet:toast (reward) — the message shown when the reward is collected. Empty shows the generic toast sentence.

stage.description: tenet:stage (task and reward) — the stage the player has to have, or the one to set. Any id, bare or namespaced: a stage exists by being granted, so there is no list to pick from and nothing to validate. With teamStage, the team's stages instead.

remove.description: tenet:stage (reward) — take the stage away instead of granting it.

teamStage.description: tenet:stage (task and reward), and the quest's requiresStage gate via requiresStageTeam — read or grant the team's stages rather than the player's own. The legacy format calls this team_stage.
